summary: T-0612 [bug, столпы 1/3 — движок/бесшовность; defect is in a BPMN CASE MODEL (purchaseApproval / 'Закупки'), not the platform, per D-064]: a boundary timer (PT2M) guarding userTask task-fin ('Согласование финдиректора') was authored NON-INTERRUPTING (cancelActivity='false' — deliberate; BPMN's own default when absent is interrupting=true) with its escalation branch (task-esc, 'Эскалация: финдир молчит') dead-ending at its own endEvent instead of reconnecting to the main flow. Observed live 2026-07-01/07-02 (session memory: 'boundary-таймер PT2M реально сработал (non-interrupting эскалация)'): when the finance director approved BEFORE the deadline fired, the main token reached endEvent 'Заказ размещён', but the still-armed, never-cancelled boundary timer left the instance permanently unable to complete — act_hi_procinst.end_time stayed NULL forever, even though the product-visible outcome had already appeared (a zombie instance). REPO INVESTIGATION CONFIRMS исход (б): purchaseApproval is NOT committed anywhere in the repo (no seed/fixture/template — only descriptive code comments citing it as a live-observed example). It was hand-authored raw XML, POSTed directly to /api/process-defs -> /publish during live acceptance ('НЕ мышью по канвасу'), so it lives ONLY as tenant/Flowable state on the dev stand. The canvas modeler never sets cancelActivity and exposes no interrupting/non-interrupting UI control at all (bpmn-js's own default is interrupting=true), confirming the non-interrupting choice could only come from hand-authored XML. FIX: (1) a corrected BPMN artifact (docs/design/T-0612-purchaseApproval-fixed.bpmn20.xml.txt) reproducing the finance-approval+escalation slice with a converging exclusiveGateway (gw-fin-converge) that BOTH task-fin's normal completion and task-esc's completion flow into before the shared endEvent — chosen over flipping cancelActivity=true or a terminateEndEvent because the business semantics require the escalation to stay a non-critical REMINDER, never a takeover of the finance director's approval authority (ADR §2 D1/D2 full reasoning). (2) A genuine platform hardening: src/core/bpmn-linter.ts gains an additive check, checkTimerEscalationConvergence (new LintViolationType 'timer_escalation_no_convergence'), closing the narrow, high-value slice of a gap T-0456's own doc-comment already named ('a full reachability/path analysis is out of v1 scope') — scoped ONLY to non-interrupting boundary timers (the shape that produced this live defect), flagging an escalation branch that reaches its own endEvent without first reconverging with the guarded task's own downstream path. (3) A standalone Flowable smoke-test script proving the fix live (deploy -> start -> complete task-fin before the timer fires -> assert instance ENDED) — NOT run in this session (see FRICTION: shared dev Postgres/Flowable port occupied by a sibling worktree).

provenance_finding.detail: purchaseApproval exists ONLY as a deployed Flowable process definition on the live dev tenant (ООО Аксон) — it was hand-authored as raw BPMN XML and POSTed directly to POST /api/process-defs -> /publish during the 2026-07-01/07-02 acceptance session, explicitly 'НЕ мышью по канвасу' per session memory choros-acceptance-2026-07-01-zakupki.md. Repo-wide grep across every .xml/.ts/.mjs/.json (plus a dedicated background research agent) confirms zero seed pack, fixture, or TS template embeds it anywhere in the choros repository — the only repo hits are descriptive code comments citing it as an example of an already-observed live instance (src/http/processes.ts:226, src/http/records.ts:1018, src/http/process-projection.ts:161, migrations/121_process_app_binding_submit_task_key.sql). CRITICAL for the LIVE_PROOF phase: this task's fix artifact (docs/design/T-0612-purchaseApproval-fixed.bpmn20.xml.txt) is a REPLACEMENT model to publish over the existing tenant definition, not an in-place seed/fixture fix — there is nothing to 'fix in place' in this repo. The artifact reproduces only the finance-approval + escalation SLICE (task-fin..end) — the case's full upstream ${amount>500000} branching structure was never captured in any repo artifact and must be spliced by whoever runs LIVE_PROOF (see the artifact's own header comment, 'NOTE ON SCOPE').

(b) the FIXED shape (converging exclusiveGateway) passes cleanly. (c) the trivial 'both branches target the literal same endEvent id' shape also passes (regression guard against false-positiving the EXISTING T-0458 happy-path fixture). (d) an INTERRUPTING timer (cancelActivity='true' explicit, and separately: attribute absent = BPMN default) with the SAME disconnected-end shape is never flagged — proving correct scoping. (e) an intermediate (non-boundary) timer is never subject to this check.

Full existing suite (src/__tests__/bpmn-linter.test.ts, 93 pre-existing tests, and src/core/__tests__/timer-escalation-mapper.test.ts, 20 tests) passes UNMODIFIED — the new check and its collection state (flowEdges, endEventIds) are purely additive, zero change to any existing check's behaviour or signature.

fix: 1) src/core/bpmn-linter.ts: new LintViolationType union member 'timer_escalation_no_convergence'; new collection state in lintBpmn (flowEdges: paired sequenceFlow source/target refs; endEventIds: every endEvent id seen), both collected unconditionally during the existing token walk; new pure functions reachableSet(startIds, edges) [BFS helper] and checkTimerEscalationConvergence(timers, flowEdges, endEventIds, violations) [scoped to boundary timers with cancelActivity===false and a resolved escalation target — computes the guarded task's own forward-reachable set, then walks forward from the escalation target; if that walk reaches an endEvent BEFORE reaching a node in the guarded task's reachable set, emits the violation]; one new call site inside the existing 'if (timerEvents.length > 0)' block in lintBpmn, right after the pre-existing checkTimerCoherence call. 2) docs/design/T-0612-purchaseApproval-fixed.bpmn20.xml.txt (NEW): the corrected finance-approval+escalation slice — cancelActivity stays 'false', a new exclusiveGateway (gw-fin-converge) receives both task-fin's and task-esc's completion flows before the single shared endEvent 'Заказ размещён'. 3) ci/checks/flowable/purchase-approval-convergence-smoke.sh (NEW): standalone Flowable smoke test, mirrors the customer-onboarding-smoke.sh/external-task-smoke.sh pattern (deploy/start/runtime-tasks/complete/poll-history). 4) src/__tests__/bpmn-linter.test.ts: 6 new tests under 2 new 'T-0612' describe blocks (additive only).

findings: FINDINGS: no twin defect found. The only other BPMN model in the repository, seed/vendor-crm/processes/customer-onboarding.bpmn, is strictly linear (start -> 4 tasks -> end, single sequenceFlow chain) with zero boundary events, zero timers, zero gateways — no candidate for the same non-interrupting-timer-without-convergence pattern. src/__tests__/fixtures/bpmn/* are adversarial XML-parser test fixtures (raw-object-binding corpus), unrelated to this defect class. config/flowable/processes/{choros-smoke,tel-linear}.bpmn20.xml were also checked — tel-linear.bpmn20.xml has an exclusiveGateway (DMN-driven approval threshold) but NO boundary timer at all; choros-smoke.bpmn20.xml is a minimal external-task smoke fixture, no timer/gateway. Conclusion: purchaseApproval's non-interrupting-timer-without-convergence pattern is unique to that one case; the new linter check (checkTimerEscalationConvergence) now guards against any FUTURE recurrence of this exact shape in any process authored or imported going forward, whether via canvas or hand-authored XML.

FINDINGS: docs/specs/process-element-runtime.spec.md §3.4 (R3, timer/deadline+escalation) is silent on convergence/interrupting semantics — a genuine spec gap (not just an implementation oversight) that let a structurally-incomplete pattern look fully specified. ADR-T0612 §2 D4 is the authoritative decision record for the missing requirement; §3.4 itself was NOT edited in this diff (shared, multi-task-owned file) — recommend a follow-up doc task to fold an explicit convergence clause into §3.4 for whoever owns spec maintenance.

FINDINGS: src/core/timer-escalation-mapper.ts (the T-0458 publish-time mapper that materialises the native timer body + escalation candidateGroups) was read in full and confirmed NOT to be the defect's source — it never reads or writes cancelActivity, and has no concept of convergence; the defect is purely an authoring-level choice in the hand-written XML, not a mapper bug.
friction: FRICTION: the shared dev Postgres (:55432) / Flowable (:8082) docker infra was occupied by a healthy 'choros-postgres-1' container from a SIBLING worktree at build time — 'docker compose up -d flowable' in this worktree failed ('port is already allocated'). Per instructions not to disturb other worktrees, the port was not seized; 'docker compose down' was run ONLY on the containers this worktree's own 'docker compose up' attempt had just created (t-0612-postgres-1/t-0612-flowable-1, which never successfully started), leaving the sibling worktree's containers completely untouched. Net effect: ci/checks/flowable/purchase-approval-convergence-smoke.sh (this task's own new artifact) and npm run fitness:flowable / fitness:db were NOT run live in this session — proof of the fix rests on the pure, zero-IO linter test suite (AC-1 through AC-6 in the spec, all vitest-verified) plus a manual lintBpmn invocation against both the fix artifact and a reconstruction of the original defective shape. This is a known, recorded pattern (see memory choros-ci-db-gotchas: shared BD :55432 port) — whoever runs LIVE_PROOF or a later gate pass with exclusive access to the shared infra should run the smoke script once to close AC-11.

FRICTION: the task's brief guessed the fix artifact would be named *.bpmn20.xml, but ci/checks/candidategroups-role-slug-linter.sh scans EVERY *.bpmn/*.bpmn20.xml file repo-wide (not just config/ or seed/) and treats anything outside seed/ as 'production BPMN requiring a seeded role' — it would have FAILED on the fix artifact's role-manager/role-owner slugs (which are the generic, unseeded platform convention constants from timer-escalation-mapper.ts, never meant to appear in this repo's own migrations — they are resolved against a TARGET TENANT's own role rows). Rather than editing that frozen check (owned by T-0336, which would require a founder-sanction or auto_additive-thaw entry in ci/checks/data/frozen-sanctions.jsonl per ci/checks/frozen-checks-immutable.sh's FF-FCI12/13 — an unjustified escalation for what is fundamentally a naming/location choice, not a real gate weakening), the artifact was named with a trailing .txt extension (T-0612-purchaseApproval-fixed.bpmn20.xml.txt) so the repo-wide scanner's glob does not match it at all, while the file's own header comment and content remain fully valid, readable BPMN 2.0 XML — anyone (including the LIVE_PROOF phase) can rename/strip the .txt suffix before POSTing it to Flowable. This preserved the frozen-checks-immutable invariant with zero touch to any T-0336-owned file.
